disclaimer: General first-aid guidance only. It does not replace emergency services or certified training. Local practices vary: follow the emergency operator and local authorities.

topics.title: Scene safety and calling for help
topics.summary: Protect yourself first, check what happened, and get professional help early.
steps: Stop and look for traffic, fire, electricity, unstable structures, violence, smoke, gas, water, or other danger.
Do not enter or remain in an unsafe place. Move the person only when leaving them would expose them to immediate danger.
Call the local emergency number or ask a specific person to call. State the location, hazards, number of people, and what you see.
Follow the operator’s instructions. Use gloves or a barrier if available, and give only the help you can provide safely.
warnings: Local emergency numbers and recommended practices vary.

topics.title: Unresponsive and not breathing normally
topics.summary: Call emergency services immediately and follow the operator. Start CPR only according to your training or their instructions.
steps: Make sure the scene is safe. Shout and gently tap the person to check for a response.
Call the local emergency number, put the phone on speaker, and send someone for an AED if one is available.
Check whether the person is breathing normally. Gasping or irregular breaths are not normal breathing.
Follow the operator. If trained, or instructed by the operator, begin CPR and use the AED as prompted. Continue until the person breathes normally, help takes over, or the scene becomes unsafe.
warnings: Do not delay the emergency call.
CPR technique differs for adults, children, and infants; follow your training and the operator.

topics.title: Severe bleeding
topics.summary: Call for emergency help and apply firm, continuous direct pressure.
steps: Check scene safety and call the local emergency number.
If available, put on gloves. Place gauze or a clean cloth directly over the wound.
Press firmly and continuously with both hands. If blood soaks through, add more material on top without removing the first layer.
Keep the person warm and still. Continue pressure until help takes over or the bleeding stops.
warnings: Do not remove deeply embedded objects; press around them.
Use a tourniquet only if trained or directed by the emergency operator.

topics.title: Burns
topics.summary: Stop the burning and cool the burn with cool running water.
steps: Make the scene safe and stop contact with the heat source without putting yourself at risk.
Remove jewelry or loose clothing near the burn unless stuck to the skin.
Cool the burn under cool running water for 20 minutes when possible. Keep the rest of the person warm.
Loosely cover with a clean, non-stick dressing or plastic film and seek emergency help for severe, large, deep, electrical, chemical, airway, face, hand, joint, or genital burns.
warnings: Do not use ice, grease, butter, creams, or toothpaste.
Do not break blisters or pull off material stuck to skin.

topics.title: Choking
topics.summary: If the person cannot cough, speak, or breathe, call emergency services and follow the operator.
steps: If the person can cough or speak, encourage coughing and watch closely.
If they cannot cough, speak, or breathe, call the local emergency number immediately or direct someone else to call.
Follow the operator and use only the choking actions appropriate to the person that you were trained to perform.
If the person becomes unresponsive, lower them safely, follow the operator, and begin CPR only according to training or instructions.
warnings: Techniques differ for adults, pregnant people, children, and infants.
Do not perform blind finger sweeps.

topics.title: Earthquake and debris
topics.summary: Avoid unstable structures and protect breathing while waiting for rescuers.
steps: During shaking, drop, cover, and hold on. Stay away from windows and heavy objects.
After shaking, expect aftershocks. Check for fire, gas, electricity, broken glass, and unstable walls before moving.
If trapped, cover your mouth and nose with cloth, avoid kicking up dust, and signal with tapping, a whistle, light, or phone. Shout only as a last resort.
Do not move heavy debris or enter damaged structures unless authorities say it is safe. Call or message emergency services when possible and follow local instructions.
warnings: Do not light flames where gas may be leaking.
Moving debris can cause collapse or worsen hidden injuries.
